prerequisites: Mechanics: Contents of the Statics lecture
Mathematics: Trigonometry, Algebra, Basics of differential and integral calculus, simple differential equations
Strength of Materials: Elasticity of beams

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the importance of kinematics and kinetics in engineering. They can set up and describe the equations of motion for simple bodies / mechanical constructions and create analogies using practical examples.

Students can confidently apply the fundamental methods of Technical Mechanics (free-body diagram, kinematic conditions, determination of forces/moments, determination of equations of motion) to simple movements of individual bodies or assemblies with one degree of freedom.

Students can analyze one- and two-dimensional accelerated movements of rigid bodies, and set up and evaluate energy balances for moving bodies. Students who have successfully completed this module know the possibilities and limitations of calculating one- and two-dimensional movements with elementary methods.
Students are able to abstract a mechanical construction in such a way that it can be calculated for mechanical design using the learned methods and its movement can be analyzed.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the planar motion of a rigid body
Work-energy theorem and conservation of energy
Angular momentum and angular momentum theorem
assessment_rules: The graded examination is a written exam (Klausur). The duration and scope of the exam are specified in the current study regulations.
